# Issue tracker: GitHub

This repository's tickets, specs, wayfinder maps and miss records are GitHub issues in
`Habit130/kev`. Sessions use the `gh` CLI, as the agent account, and pass
`--repo Habit130/kev` on every call, since the target is otherwise ambiguous.

## Conventions

- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --repo Habit130/kev --title "..." --body-file <file>`,
  with `--label "..."` for each label.
- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <n> --repo Habit130/kev --comments`; add
  `--json number,title,body,labels,assignees,comments` for fields.
- **List issues**: `gh issue list --repo Habit130/kev --state open --label <label> --json number,title,labels,assignees`
- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <n> --repo Habit130/kev --body-file <file>`
- **Apply or remove a label**: `gh issue edit <n> --repo Habit130/kev --add-label "..."`, or
  `--remove-label "..."`.
- **Close an issue**: `gh issue close <n> --repo Habit130/kev --comment "..."`

GitHub shares one number space between issues and PRs: resolve a bare `#42` with
`gh pr view 42 --repo Habit130/kev` first, then `gh issue view 42 --repo Habit130/kev`.

## Sub-issues and blocking

- **Make a sub-issue**: `gh issue create --repo Habit130/kev --parent <parent> ...` creates
  one; `gh issue edit <parent> --repo Habit130/kev --add-sub-issue <child>,<child>` adds
  existing issues. A spec's tickets are its sub-issues.
- **Blocking** is GitHub's native issue dependencies: `--blocked-by <n>,<n>` on
  `gh issue create`, or `gh issue edit <n> --repo Habit130/kev --add-blocked-by <blocker>`
  (`--remove-blocked-by` to undo) on an existing issue.
- **Read both**: `gh issue view <n> --repo Habit130/kev --json parent,subIssues,blockedBy,blocking`.
  A ticket is unblocked once every blocker under `blockedBy` is done: a PR-delivered
  ticket has merged, its PR closing it; a results-comment ticket (`builder.md`) is closed
  as completed. A wayfinder ticket is unblocked once every blocker is closed.

## Tickets

- **Dispatch**: `triage-labels.md`, `ready-for-agent`. A spec approved for whole-spec
  delivery is dispatched as one, its tickets with it (`planner.md`, Specs).
- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --repo Habit130/kev --add-assignee @me`. It is the Builder's
  first write, and it posts no comment. An assigned ticket is claimed. A Builder on a
  whole-spec delivery claims the spec and each of its tickets (`builder.md`).
- **A published ticket is frozen** (`planner.md`, Tickets). It carries no digests or contract
  versions, since GitHub keeps the body's edit history. Evidence and records go in comments.
- **Closing**: results-comment tickets follow `builder.md`, Results-comment tickets.
  For PR delivery, a PR's `Closes #<n>` lines close those issues when habit merges it
  (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`).

## Pull requests as a triage surface

**PRs as a request surface: no.** `triage` reads this flag. An outside PR, by anyone but the
repository owner or the agent account, fails the governance gate, and when habit wants its
change a Builder re-lands it (`builder.md`, Outside PRs). So `triage` handles issues only.

## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"

Create a GitHub issue, as in **Create an issue**.

## When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"

Read it as in **Read an issue**, comments included.

## Wayfinding operations

Used by `wayfinder`. The **map** is one issue, and its **child** issues are its tickets.

- **Map**: an issue labelled `wayfinder:map`.
- **Child ticket**: a sub-issue of the map labelled `wayfinder:<type>`, where type is
  `research`, `prototype`, `grilling` or `task`.
- **Blocking**: native issue dependencies, as in **Sub-issues and blocking**.
- **Frontier**: the map's open children with no open blocker and no assignee. List them with
  `gh issue view <map> --repo Habit130/kev --json subIssues`, then read each open child's
  `blockedBy` and `assignees`. First in map order wins.
- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --repo Habit130/kev --add-assignee @me`, the session's first
  write.
- **Resolve**: comment the answer, close the ticket, then add a one-line gist and link to the
  map's Decisions so far.

## Miss records

A miss is governance letting through something its rules should have stopped. Each one gets
one issue labelled `miss`, in the repository where it happened. Who records which miss is in
the role files and `AGENTS.md`, Secrets; this section is how.

- **Open one.** First list the open records:
  `gh issue list --repo Habit130/kev --label miss --state open --json number,title,body`.
  When one already covers the miss, comment there instead. While a `red-default-branch`
  record is open, the default branch counts as still red, and no second one opens. Otherwise
  `gh issue create --repo Habit130/kev --label miss --title "..." --body-file <file>`, in
  the format below, with `miss` as its only label.
- **Skip triage.** A miss record never takes a triage label, and `triage` leaves `miss` issues
  to their `retro`. A bug keeps its own issue, which goes through triage as usual and which
  the record links.
- **Close it** only after its `retro`, quoting habit's decision:
  `gh issue close <n> --repo Habit130/kev --comment "..."`.
- **An exposed credential** is named by its type and location only, never its value, in the
  title, the body and every comment.

### Format

The title is `Miss: <kind>, <category>`, followed by ` in #<n>` when the record names a
merged PR.

The body opens with these six field lines, in this order, each starting with its name, so a
script can fill and read them. Free detail may follow after a blank line.

```text
Merged PR: <#n | none>
Kind: <escape | process miss>
Category: <category>
Observed: <one line: what was seen, with links and full commit SHAs>
Found by: <Merge watch | Planner | Builder | Reviewer | habit>
Bug issue: <#n | none>
```

- **Merged PR**: the merged PR the miss is about; for a revert, the reverted PR. `none` when
  no merged PR is involved.
- **Kind**: `escape`, a problem that got past governance; or `process miss`, a governance
  rule that wasn't followed, with nothing catching it before the merge.
- **Category**: one of the table's.
- **Found by**: Merge watch; the role of the session that found it; or habit, when habit
  noticed it and told a session.
- **Bug issue**: for `bug`, the bug's own issue; otherwise `none`.

| Category | Kind | Observed names |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `red-default-branch` | escape | the push-triggered workflow run on the default branch concluding `failure`, `cancelled`, `timed_out` or `startup_failure`: its workflow, run link and commit |
| `revert` | escape | the PR that reverted the merged PR, and whether its body had a `Reverts:` line |
| `missing-review` | process miss | the declared tier, the merged head, and each missing review by its Merge summary kind (`review.md`), or `merge-summary` |
| `push-without-pr` | process miss | the commit pushed to the default branch with no merged PR |
| `bug` | escape | the bug traced to the merged PR |
| `exposed-credential` | escape | the credential's type and location |
| `other` | either | anything else, such as an outside change that broke a governance run |

### Examples

A process miss Merge watch records, titled `Miss: process miss, missing-review in #42`:

```text
Merged PR: #42
Kind: process miss
Category: missing-review
Observed: Merged head 1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d7e8f9a0b, declared medium, lacks: reviewer, merge-summary.
Found by: Merge watch
Bug issue: none
```

An escape a Planner records at triage, titled `Miss: escape, bug in #37`:

```text
Merged PR: #37
Kind: escape
Category: bug
Observed: #51 reports exports dropping entries logged after midnight; triage traced it to #37's date handling.
Found by: Planner
Bug issue: #51
```

An escape with no merged PR, titled `Miss: escape, exposed-credential`:

```text
Merged PR: none
Kind: escape
Category: exposed-credential
Observed: An API token for the sync service, in a review comment on the open PR #58.
Found by: Builder
Bug issue: none
```
